title: Height of a valuation is unchanged by algebraic extension
statement: Let $E/K$ be an algebraic extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-algebraic-element]. Let $V\subseteq E$ be a valuation ring of $E$, meaning a subring such that for every $a\in E^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Put $A=V\cap K$. Then $A$ is a valuation ring of $K$ and contraction of prime ideals gives an order isomorphism from the prime ideals of $V$ onto the prime ideals of $A$, ordered by inclusion. In particular $V$ and $A$ have the same height, where height is the supremum of the lengths of finite strictly increasing chains of prime ideals; either both heights are finite or both are infinite.

source.place: §2.1, p. 7: correspondence of prime ideals with convex subgroups of the value group, and the finite-extension fundamental inequality $\sum_i e_{L_i/k}f_{L_i/k}\le[L:k]$ at the foot of p. 7, shortly before Lemma 2.1.2 (p. 8); algebraic height invariance is the consequence for the union of finite subextensions.
